A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Local Constrained Bayesian Optimization (LCBO). Their main text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic, engineering-design, and HalfCheetah experiments, plus a batch-schedule ablation in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds component and penalty-schedule ablations and an empirical analysis of SCBO restarts.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same exploration acquisition, repeated evaluations, quadratic-penalty surrogate, and projected gradient update. The Z2 wording and newly stated one-sided inequality handling clarify implementation without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 25D, 50D, and 100D synthetic problems, 25D truss design, 50D beam design, and 102D HalfCheetah. The added analyses reuse the truss and 50D synthetic tasks without introducing new task requirements or environments.

E2.justification: CEI, EPBO, SCBO, and HDsafeBO remain the external baselines. New ablation comparisons add LCBO variants without individual auxiliary components and variants with fixed penalties of 1, 10, 100, and 1000 in Figures 6–7.

E3.justification: Appendices C.2–C.3 add controlled experiments that individually remove local GP fitting, local search boxes, or gradient normalization, and compare growing against fixed penalties. Existing benchmark initialization, evaluation budgets, noise, metrics, and batch-schedule protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 examines only batch scheduling. V2 retains that study as Appendix C.1 and substantially expands diagnostic evidence through component ablations, penalty-schedule sensitivity tests, and SCBO restart analysis addressing the proposed explanation of trust-region stagnation.

E5.justification: The ten-run median/interquartile-range benchmark reporting and five-seed batch-schedule study are retained. Figures 6–7 explicitly follow Figure 1's reporting conventions; the added restart summaries also use medians and interquartile ranges rather than introducing a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and batch-schedule results are retained. Figures 6–7 add substantive findings about component removal and weak versus excessive fixed penalties. Appendix B newly reports at least two SCBO restarts in every truss run, with first and second restart medians of 350 and 747 evaluations and interquartile ranges of 338–383 and 657–756.

T1.justification: Remark 5.4 replaces the claimed equivalence to MFCQ and strict comparison with LICQ with an LICQ implication and a connection to the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz condition. Assumption 5.3 itself, the convergence bounds, and the entire Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: extending local BO to constraints, polynomial dimensional dependence of KKT convergence, and superior benchmark performance. The new analyses support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix B develops the stagnation mechanism while explicitly acknowledging that trust-region methods can recover through restarts; the concern becomes their cost under limited budgets. Appendices C.2–C.3 add substantive interpretations attributing gains to the core penalty mechanism and explaining normalization, penalty trade-offs, and robustness without task-specific tuning.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly specifies standard one-sided penalties for inequality constraints. Hardware, GP fitting details, normalization, and Table 1 hyperparameters are retained. The HalfCheetah objective and energy threshold added to the main text were already documented in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: V2 adds Tang et al. (2025) and Brunzema and Trimpe (2026) when discussing second-order local BO, adds Nesterov et al. (2018) for smoothness, and removes Robinson (1976) alongside the revised constraint-qualification statement. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. V2 adds Section 6.4 and a mechanism appendix, reorganizes the previous batch study into an expanded ablation appendix, and renumbers the setup appendices. Other edits clarify terminology and update affiliations, correspondence, publication information, and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: V2 adds a substantial mechanism illustration in Figure 3 and two paired ablation displays in Figures 6–7. Main Figures 1–2 remain unchanged; the old batch plots become Figures 4–5 with minor resizing, and the unchanged hyperparameter table is relocated.

improvement.justification: The new restart measurements and targeted ablations strengthen explanations that v1 supported mainly through benchmark curves, while the revised theoretical qualification and implementation clarification improve precision. These are useful, incremental gains: the central algorithm, proofs, and benchmark results remain unchanged, and the additional diagnostic evidence concerns two retained tasks.
